competing_candidates.what_would_kill_it: If the thermal compensation algorithm is enabled with a calibrated gain, the measured tool-center drift at the 3-hour mark will be less than 10 microns, compared to >40 microns without compensation, under constant load conditions.

competing_candidates.mechanism: Passive thermal symmetry design, which minimizes differential expansion by ensuring the spindle assembly expands uniformly along its central axis rather than laterally. competing_candidates.mechanism: Active thermal equilibration, where the spindle is pre-heated or held at a constant temperature to match the thermal state of the cutting environment, thereby eliminating the temperature delta that causes expansion. competing_candidates.intervention: Replace the existing spindle support structure with a symmetric, thermally isolated bearing housing that ensures equal temperature distribution on opposite sides of the spindle, or add a thermal barrier/shield to reduce asymmetric heat ingress from the coolant or cutting zone.
competing_candidates.what_would_kill_it: If a symmetric thermal shield or housing is installed, the lateral drift (X/Y axis) will decrease by more than 50% compared to the baseline asymmetric condition, while the axial drift remains unchanged, resulting in a net tool-center error <10 microns.

competing_candidates.mechanism: Active thermal equilibration, where the spindle is pre-heated or held at a constant temperature to match the thermal state of the cutting environment, thereby eliminating the temperature delta that causes expansion. This domain knowledge principle (thermal equilibrium minimizes drift) is driven by the record's evidence of a specific time-domain failure ("3-hour shift") and the need to avoid stopping for recalibration.
competing_candidates.intervention: Install a Peltier element or fluid-based heater/cooler loop in the spindle housing that actively maintains the spindle at a target temperature (e.g., 22°C) regardless of cutting heat input, or implement a pre-heat cycle that runs during setup.
competing_candidates.what_would_kill_it: If the active thermal control is set to hold the spindle at 22°C, the drift curve will become flat near 0 microns after a short stabilization period, whereas the uncontrolled spindle shows a monotonic increase to 40 microns.
